full_judgment: 2. Facts that have given rise to this Rule, in brief, are that the plaintiff brought Title Suit No. 173 of 1961 in the Court of the then Munsif, Cox's Bazar against the defendants for declaration of his title to the suit land and for khas possession after demolition of the structures standing thereon. The suit was contested by the defendant Nos. 1-3 by filing a written statement. After hearing the trial Court decreed the suit of the plaintiff by his judgment and decree dated 14-1-1964. Against the aforesaid judgment and decree the defendants 1-3 preferred Title Appeal No. 86 of 1963 in the Court of the District Judge, Chittagong. On transfer the appeal was heard by the Subordinate Judge, 3rd Court, Chittagong who by his judgment and decree dated 10-2-1964 dismissed the appeal and affirmed the judgment and decree of the trial Court. After disposal of the aforesaid Title Appeal the plaintiff put the decree to execution by starting Execution Case No. 70 of 1964 in the Court of the Senior Assistant Judge (then Munsif), Cox's Bazar. Defendant-appellants 1-3 preferred Second Appeal No. 583 of 1964/Civil Rule No. 213(S) of 1964 before the then East Pakistan High Court and the High Court was pleased to stay all further proceedings of other Execution Case No. 70 of 1964 passed in Civil Rule No. 213(S) of 1964 on 4-12-1964 till disposal of the second appeal. The Second Appeal No. 583 of 1964 was dismissed for default on 4-8-78. As the decree holder Md Abul Quashem, and the judgment debtor-defendants 1-3 died leaving behind their legal heirs, the said legal heirs were duly substituted in the Execution Case No. 70 of 1964 by the Assistant Judge, Cox's Bazar. On 27-5-1992 the heirs of the decree holder filed an application for proceeding with the execution case and the Assistant Judge, Cox's Bazar allowed the prayer of the decree holders by his order dated 27-5-1992 and fixed 3-6-1992 for taking necessary steps in the case. By an order dated 3-6-1992 the Assistant Judge directed the decree holders to deposit Taka 300.00 as fee of the Nazir. On the prayer of the Judgment debtors the Assistant Judge, Cox's Bazar appointed an Advocate Commissioner for local inspection of the suit land to ascertain if there were huts standing on the suit land and the Advocate Commissioner accordingly inspected the suit land on 28-4-1964 and submitted his report on the following day stating that there was no shop house and valuable goods on the suit land. The Nazir of the Court delivered possession of the suit land to the decree holders on 9-6-1992 and submitted his report before the Assistant Judge accordingly. The judgment debtors thereafter filed a written objection against the report of the Nazir on 10-6-1992 and 29- 6-1992 was fixed for hearing of the objection. On 29-6-1992 the judgment debtors filed an application before the Assistant Judge under section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure stating, inter alia, that the starting of the execution case on 20-5-1992 was not intimated to the judgment debtors or their Advocate and that the schedule of the decree is vague and indefinite and that the execution case in question is barred by limitation and that their possession in the suit land be restored to them.
